questions.prompt: Why is a broad codebase search a good job to delegate to a subagent?

options.text: Subagents read files faster than the main agent
The search's file-reading happens in the subagent's separate context and is discarded — only the conclusion enters the main context
The main agent isn't allowed to search

questions.explanation: It's quarantine for context pollution: the messy exploration lives and dies in the subagent. The main session pays one paragraph of budget for an answer that cost twenty files to find.

questions.prompt: What should a well-briefed subagent return?

options.text: The full text of every file it examined, for transparency
A concise conclusion: the answer, key file paths, and only load-bearing snippets

questions.explanation: Conclusions, not dumps. Returning everything it read would pour the pollution straight into the context you were protecting.

questions.prompt: Which task is NOT worth delegating to a subagent?

options.text: Sweep the whole repo to find where errors are logged
Read one specific 20-line file you already know the path of
Survey how three different modules handle validation
Hunt for all usages of a deprecated function across many directories

questions.explanation: Delegation has overhead and is justified when exploration would be broad. One known small file? Just read it — the pollution is 20 lines.

questions.prompt: This app was itself planned by agents using context isolation. Which practices does that illustrate? (select all that apply)

options.text: Planner agents spawned explorers and received summaries, not file dumps
The planning context stayed lean enough to hold the whole design
Every agent shared one giant common context for consistency
Parallel explorations ran in separate contexts without polluting each other

questions.explanation: Isolation, not sharing, is the trick (c is the anti-pattern): separate contexts explore in parallel and only distilled conclusions merge into the plan.
